summary: No fundamentals thesis is broken by evidence in the files. Every held name that was on the 11-03 menu (DPZ, IDXX, CARG, VRSN, MSCI, FAST, MSM, KR, WMT) is still there with its F-score and cfo above net income unchanged, and no flags are set on any of them. Today's -4.4% SPY drop pulled VOO (-4.6%), VTI (-4.3%), IDXX (-4.0%), MSM (-4.4%) and BTC/USD (-5.7%) down together, which is a market move and not a fundamentals break. Two decision-time marks look stale against close.json (IDXX and BTC/USD), so the stop distances the PM wrote down are too generous (see update).
update: L5 (compute distances from the latest mark): the decision text used equity $636.18 and marks that do not match close.json ($622.50). (1) IDXX: the PM re-anchored the invalidation to $630 as 'about 10% under the ~$700 mark'. close.json implies a close near $670.7 (48.26 / 0.0719 sh), after -4.0% today, so $630 is about 6% away, not 10%, and the position is +20.7% on cost. The thesis (F 8/9, cfo $1,182M vs net income $1,059M, gp_sector_pct 0.949) is intact; the stop only needs re-checking against the real close. (2) BTC/USD: the PM wrote about $79.3k with the ~$75.3k stop 5% away. close.json implies about $75.9k (13.30 / 0.000175 BTC), -5.7% today and -9.3% on cost, so the stop is under 1% away. The invalidation (10% below the $83.7k fill, about $75.3k) has not tripped on a close yet, and one day's move is not a broken thesis, but it is the nearest to tripping in the book; NFP 11-06 is next. BTC/USD is off the fundamentals menu by nature, so I have no filing evidence either way. (3) VOO/VTI: invalidations hinge on SPY closing below its 200-day (723.99 / 723.23). The PM cited a 5.46% cushion, but SPY fell about 4.4% today; I cannot verify the cushion from the files I read, so recheck it on the close mark. (4) CARG: the Q3 print is after today's close, so the fundamentals thesis (gp 1.27, cfo $295M vs net income $156M) is untested until 11-06; the written sell-on-negative-surprise plan stands. (5) Label caveats unchanged: DPZ's Staples rank is a wholesale-groceries SIC artifact and MSCI is labelled Industrials, so the Staples stack (WMT, DPZ, KR) is not diversification by label alone. MSM (-6.5% on cost, -4.4% today) remains inside its ~9% invalidation; no new filing evidence in the inputs I read.
